note: Declared route capability table. Every exported HTTP handler under web/app/api appears here, at method grain. status 'declared' requires a catalog capability key; status 'none' asserts the handler legitimately requires none and must state why; status 'pending' is W-15's burndown backlog and is ratcheted downward only. Enforced by scripts/checkRouteCapabilities.mjs (prebuild) and locked by tests/access/routeCapabilityDeclaration.test.ts (RL-10). W-14 delivers the mechanism and the pilot slice; W-15 drives pending to zero.

inherited.$comment: Handlers that entered web/app/api from OTHER programs while this branch was frozen, and are therefore not part of the Access backlog `ratchet.max_pending` bounds. The effective assertion is `pending - inherited <= max_pending`, so the program-owned backlog stays ratcheted at its committed ceiling and the ceiling is NOT raised. Every entry must still exist, still be exported, and still be `pending`: a deleted route, a removed method, or a handler that has since been classified `declared` or `none` FAILS until it is removed from this list. The list may only shrink. Nothing here asserts anything about a handler's authorization - these are W-15 backlog items awaiting OD-7 exactly like every other `pending` entry, and none of them is exempt from it. Shape follows the sibling gate scripts/checkServiceClientPrincipal.mjs, whose `baseline` list is the same idea for the same backlog.
inherited.frozen_by: Access & Identity V2 recovery onto current staging. The recovered W-14 table was authored against the route tree at merge-base 08e9dd878; 459 staging commits later 20 handlers exist that it had never seen. Audited one by one: NONE consults a catalog capability, so none can be `declared`; 10 are gated by requireAdminOrOps (membership + portal eligibility, not authorization), 7 are authenticated-only org context, 3 are public token routes whose closest siblings are themselves pending. Classifying any of them is the OD-7 conversion decision, which a recovery does not make.

POST.reason: Admission is the action-link token in the request, which IS the credential. There is no org principal to hold a capability: the recipient is a vendor or contact acting on a link mailed to them, and requiring a capability would make the route unusable by everyone it exists for. The token is the authorization boundary, and its strength is a token-lifecycle question (W-36's surface), not a capability question.
Action-link token, as consume-accept-job. Bearer admission by design; no org principal exists to carry a capability.

GET.reason: Action-link token, as consume-accept-job. Resolves what the link refers to before the recipient acts on it; the token scopes the answer.

POST.reason: The token is in the path and is the credential. Same class as action-links, different generation of the same feature — the duplication is real and is IA-8's territory, not a capability question.

GET.reason: Resolves what the path token refers to, before the recipient acts on it. Bearer admission by the token, as action/[token]/consume.

Reports the CALLER'S OWN config-assist capabilities as three booleans, computed from the caller's own access context (route.ts:14-23). It discloses no other principal's data and no org data, and gating a capability projection on the capability it projects would make the UI unable to tell a user what they cannot do. Admission (W-13 portal.access) is still required upstream. This is a reviewed assertion, not an absence.

DELETE.reason: The handler is an unconditional 405: it takes no parameters, reads no request, touches no client and returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED on every call. There is no action to authorize. This is the state's intended use — 'no gate' as an auditable assertion rather than an absence — and it is reviewable from six lines of source, which is why it is settled here instead of waiting on W-15's product decisions.

DELETE.reason: An unconditional 405, identical in shape to customer-person-role-types DELETE: no parameters, no request read, no client, NOT_IMPLEMENTED on every call. Deactivation goes through PATCH is_active=false, which stays pending because it does act.

GET.note: Recorded, not imposed. This handler already calls the very assertDocumentAccess that documents/[id]/signed-url and vendors/[id]/documents/signed-url both declare as documents.read, and already refuses on decision.outcome !== 'allowed' before the URL is minted. The table was under-reporting: it sat 'pending' while enforcing. Declaring it changes who may call this route by nothing at all, which is what makes it Director-ownable where the rest of W-15 is not. The check runs inside `if (doc)` because that is the only branch that discloses anything — the no-document fall-through returns metadata the person read already carries. POST and DELETE stay pending deliberately: they gate on ctx.role !== 'admin', which is a gate but not a capability gate, and which key replaces a raw role check is W-15's product call.

W-14 FINDING — the method grain found this. POST requires settings.users_roles; GET requires only getAdminContextCached(), i.e. portal admission. A file-grained census counts this file as gated because POST is. Whether roster read should require settings.users_roles is a product decision for W-15, not a worker's — declaring it 'none' here would assert an answer this workstream has no authority to give, so this stays 'pending'. AMENDED: the finding's DISCLOSURE half is closed. GET no longer returns every member's email address to everyone the portal admits — the address is projected against canManageUsersAndRoles (the same predicate the managing routes enforce, read a second time) and a server-computed `label` carries the naming function its consumers actually needed. Admission is deliberately unchanged, so this remains a pending declaration and not a resolved one. See lib/access/memberDirectoryProjection.ts and tests/access/memberDirectoryDisclosure.test.ts.

RESIDUAL RISK, recorded rather than resolved here: an unauthenticated write with no rate limit is an abuse surface. That is a throttling concern, not an authorization one — there is no principal to authorize — so it does not belong in this table and is not silently closed by this entry.

The org is taken from environment, never from the request, so a caller cannot steer it at another tenant — which is what would make an unauthenticated read dangerous here. Pricing and catalog data intended for anonymous display.

The custom fields flagged for public booking, for the ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID org. POST.reason: Provider callback from Resend. Admission is the Svix signature, verified against RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and the handler FAILS CLOSED — 503 when the secret is unconfigured, 400 when the signature headers are absent. The caller is a delivery provider, not a principal; there is no membership and therefore no capability. The signature is the boundary.

Twilio delivery-status callback, scoped to one provider binding. The binding's secret_ref resolves the verification token, falling back to the global TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, and the handler fails closed with 503 when no token resolves. Signature admission, as resend.
The unscoped form of the same Twilio callback, verified against the global TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN and failing closed identically.
